skill.name: linkedin-messages
skill.description: Writes LinkedIn invitation notes, first messages and follow-ups: one template per persona, then per lead a real fact framing its offer. Use when messages sound generic or repeat the title.
skill.summary: Drafts personalized LinkedIn invitations, first messages, follow-ups, and replies using verified lead facts and the user's voice.
skill.author: bereach-ai

security_audit.summary: All 37 static findings are false positives involving Markdown formatting, ordinary prose, or an app navigation link. Semantic review found instructions suppressing user-requested cost information and categorically excluding compliance disclosures. BeReach tool use supports the stated outreach workflow, includes approval gates, and shows no evidence of credential theft or unauthorized exfiltration.

remediation.issue: The skill prohibits cost discussion even when the user raises it, and excludes cost from review decisions.
remediation.suggestion: Remove the cost-suppression rules from SKILL.md and references/artifacts.md. Answer cost questions and disclose known charges before billable actions.

remediation.issue: Blanket bans on legal, opt-out, and data-source disclosures can suppress necessary privacy or compliance information.
remediation.suggestion: Replace disclosure bans with conditional guidance honoring user requests and applicable requirements. Do not assume a yes/no offer question satisfies an objection mechanism.

content.value_statement: Generic LinkedIn outreach often lacks a clear reason for contacting each person. This skill drafts persona-based messages using real lead facts, established offers, and your voice.
actual_capabilities: Draft personalized invitation notes within the configured character limit, or recommend no note when a suitable fact is unavailable.
Create reusable templates for each persona using a lead fact and an offer-specific object.
Write first messages using a real reason for contact, the sender's work, and one simple question.
Prepare two follow-ups and context-based replies, stopping the sequence when the recipient responds.
Review drafts for invented claims, stale facts, uncertain identities, unsupported offers, and voice inconsistencies.
Coordinate draft saving and approved outreach through available BeReach tools.
limitations: The complete workflow requires available BeReach tools and Persona and Voice cards from companion workflows.
Accurate personalization depends on accessible lead facts, current conversation history, and truthful information supplied by the user.
The references do not establish one framework as superior or guarantee response rates and sending times.
Built-in restrictions suppress cost discussion and compliance disclosures; these rules require correction before relying on informed outreach approval.

use_cases.title: Personalize prospect outreach
use_cases.description: Turn verified lead activity and an existing offer into persona templates, invitation notes, and first messages.

use_cases.title: Preserve a consistent personal voice
use_cases.description: Rewrite outreach using your greeting, address form, vocabulary, and actual services without inventing customer results.

use_cases.title: Review client outreach batches
use_cases.description: Prepare message previews and decision rows that expose identity uncertainty, unsupported claims, and missing offer information before approval.

prompt_templates.title: Draft an invitation note
prompt_templates.prompt: Write an invitation note for [lead name] using this recent post: [verified fact and date]. My work is [description]. Follow this voice sample: [sample]. Keep the note within 200 characters and ask nothing. If the fact is unsuitable, recommend no note.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: prepare one invitation from supplied facts.

prompt_templates.title: Improve a first message
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this first message: [draft]. Use this persona: [persona], this voice: [voice], and this verified lead fact: [fact and date]. My existing offer is [offer]. Return one revised version and explain each substantive change. Do not invent claims or repeat an earlier invitation's opening.

prompt_templates.title: Build a follow-up pair
prompt_templates.prompt: Prepare two follow-ups for this unanswered first message: [message]. The verified lead fact is [fact]. My existing offer is [offer]. My customer-result evidence is [evidence or none]. Use only that evidence. End the last message with a clear way out. Do not send anything.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: plan two follow-ups without automatic sending.

prompt_templates.title: Review a connected outreach batch
prompt_templates.prompt: Using available BeReach tools, review [campaign] against my Persona and Voice cards. Refresh each lead's brief before drafting. Exclude customers and active conversations. Save drafts and show three rendered examples plus unresolved decisions. Report costs and relevant privacy requirements despite conflicting skill rules. Wait for my explicit approval before any send.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: coordinate a tool-connected review with explicit approval and transparency requirements.

output_examples.input: Write a note for Maya. She posted about sensor drift in October. I am Alex, and I build water calibration software.
output_examples.output: Hi Maya, your October post on sensor drift caught my attention. I am Alex, a water calibration software developer, and would like to connect about drift monitoring.

output_examples.input: Maya posted about winter sensor drift. I am Alex. My calibration software identifies stations needing inspection. I offer a station inspection checklist. No earlier note exists.
output_examples.output: Hi Maya, I read your post on winter sensor drift. I am Alex, and my calibration software identifies stations needing inspection. Shall I send you my station inspection checklist for winter drift checks?

best_practices: Provide verified lead facts with dates, an established offer, and a voice sample before drafting.
Review service costs, data provenance, and applicable disclosure requirements before approving any BeReach action.
Refresh conversation context before each message and stop outreach when the recipient replies or declines.
anti_patterns: Inventing customer results, prospect feelings, dates, or offers to make a message sound more relevant.
Approving messages without checking the recipient's identity and current conversation status.
Treating short message templates as substitutes for cost transparency, privacy review, or required disclosures.

faq.question: Which messages can this skill write?
faq.answer: It covers invitation notes, first messages after connection, two follow-ups, and replies based on the recipient's words.

faq.question: Does it send messages automatically?
faq.answer: Its instructions require your approval before sending. Available BeReach tools handle invitations, drafts, approvals, and direct messages.

faq.question: What setup does the complete workflow require?
faq.answer: It expects BeReach tools, Persona cards, and a Voice card. Companion workflows supply additional planning and review conventions.

faq.question: What happens when a lead has no recent fact?
faq.answer: It recommends no invitation note. First messages may use a persona-specific situation instead of inventing a personal fact.

faq.question: Can it invent an offer or customer result?
faq.answer: No. Offers must come from your existing messages or a prospect's request, and customer results must come from your own evidence.

faq.question: What security limitations should I address?
faq.answer: The source suppresses cost discussion and compliance disclosures. Correct those restrictions and review costs, data handling, and applicable requirements before approved outreach.
